headline_marked: [[Meta and Microsoft slash Claude AI usage]] by employees, pivot to internal tools
headline: Meta and Microsoft slash Claude AI usage by employees, pivot to internal tools
summary: The tech giants are reducing internal spending on Anthropic's Claude AI, shifting focus to their own proprietary coding assistants like GitHub Copilot and MetaCode.
details: Meta and Microsoft are significantly cutting down employee use of Anthropic's Claude AI, as reported by The Information on October 5. This move prioritizes internal expenditure and workforce processes, shifting towards their own proprietary coding instruments.

Microsoft's anticipated internal spending on Anthropic tech, once over $1 billion annually, has dropped by more than a third. Management directed employees to use Microsoft tools like GitHub Copilot and OpenAI frameworks instead.

Monthly AI spending limits in Microsoft's cloud and AI sector have reportedly been reduced from $100,000 per employee to about $10,000 in most cases. This budgetary shift has disappointed some engineers who previously had more flexibility.

At Meta, the number of Claude Code users reportedly fell from 60,000 to about 30,000 this year. This decline is mainly due to Meta's strategic pivot to its own AI solutions, including MetaCode and Muse Code.
MetaCode now has over 30,000 internal users, and Muse Code has over 6,000 employee users. Meta began external testing of Muse Code with clients in August.
Despite the reduction in users, Meta reportedly allocated over $105 million to Claude Code over a 28-day period, showing that reduced user count doesn't always mean less spending.

This transition to different coding assistants still poses cybersecurity risks related to automated access to sensitive files and credentials. Previous analyses highlighted vulnerabilities in Claude Code and Microsoft's offerings, which were later rectified.

These incidents underscore the importance of strict permissions, trusted project settings, and thorough evaluations of AI-generated actions. Anthropic's reported $65 billion annualized revenue pace indicates continued strong demand for its services externally.
